Q1: How should this heal proceed when the failed step's log is unavailable?
Choices:
A. Make the step report which command failed: each command in `install-opencode/action.yml` gets its own `::error::install-opencode: stage=<npm_install|version_check|models_refresh|run_help> rc=<n>` line. Exit behaviour stays the same (still fails closed, no retry), and a contract test pins each stage's error line by simulating that stage failing. This makes the next occurrence diagnosable; it does not claim to fix a root cause. (RECOMMENDED)
B. Supply the step log from run 37862635273 in an `/answer` (or name the failing command) so the plan can target the actual root cause with a reproducing regression test.
C. Close this heal issue as not actionable (no code change), and rely on the lineage cap and escalation if the failure happens again.
Q2: If the failing stage turns out to be (or is presumed to be) `opencode models --refresh`, the network warm-up of the models.dev cache, should that stage stay fatal?
Choices:
A. Keep it fatal: a failed cache warm-up keeps failing the step, matching the current fail-closed behaviour. (RECOMMENDED)
B. Make only the cache warm-up non-fatal: log a `::warning::` and continue, while the install, version-check and `run --help` checks stay fatal. **Note:** this may count as weakening a check under the issue's fix constraints. Choose it only with Q1:B evidence that the refresh is the failing stage.
